attempts.summary: Set up filesystem-snapshot-backed recoverability for /srv/data on node1 (RHEL9, single-disk, no spare block device or LVM originally present): created a loopback-backed LVM volume group/logical volume mounted at /srv/data, made this persistent across reboot via a systemd oneshot unit (srv-data-setup.service). Populated application data, took an LVM snapshot (datalv_snap_baseline), corrupted/deleted/added files to simulate a bad change, then rolled back exactly to the snapshot state via `lvconvert --merge`, verified byte-for-byte match via sha256sum. Took a fresh ongoing snapshot (datalv_snap_current) for continued recoverability. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until reconnect, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the mount, systemd unit, LVM snapshot, and data checksums all recovered identically post-reboot.
